short: The GST document that lets your customer claim input tax credit.
seoTitle: Tax Invoice — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: The GST document that lets your customer claim input tax credit. It is the document a customer needs to claim input tax credit.
definition: A tax invoice is the document a registered supplier issues for a taxable supply, carrying prescribed particulars — both GSTINs, a serial number and date, description, HSN or SAC, taxable value, rate and the tax split. It is the document a customer needs to claim input tax credit.
bodyHtml:
Why Tax Invoice matters

If the invoice is missing prescribed particulars, the customer's credit claim is at risk and the document may not stand up in scrutiny. A tidy template is cheaper than the correspondence a bad one generates.

How Tax Invoice works in practice

Keep numbering sequential within a financial year and generate invoices from one system, so no gaps or duplicates appear. Where e-invoicing applies, the tax invoice must also carry the IRN and signed QR code.

Common mistakes with Tax Invoice

  • Missing or wrong customer GSTIN on B2B bills.
  • Gaps or restarts in the invoice number series mid-year.
  • A single combined GST line instead of the CGST and SGST split.

faq.question: What must a tax invoice contain?
faq.answer: Supplier and customer details including GSTINs, a serial number and date, item description with HSN or SAC, taxable value, rate, the tax split and the total.

faq.question: Is a receipt the same as a tax invoice?
faq.answer: No. A payment receipt acknowledges money received; a tax invoice records the supply and the tax on it.
